blocks.intro: Königsberg, on the river Pregel: two islands, four neighbourhoods, seven bridges. Eight homes need a designer.
blocks.name: Königsberg
blocks.subtitle: Seven bridges, eight homes

mechanic_intro.body:
Every apartment has a tenant, and every tenant has needs. They are listed in the bar at the bottom: a tick means the apartment already provides it, a cross means it doesn't.

Marisol's family can cook, wash and store things here, but there is nowhere to sleep and nowhere to sit.

Open Furniture (top left, or press F). The catalogue opens on what the tenant still needs: buy a bed and something to sit on. Click the floor to put each one down. Press R to rotate while placing.

When every need is ticked, the apartment is ready to rent.
mechanic_intro.title: Welcome to Make It Fit

tenant.flavor: A 64 m² beach apartment for the whole family. The kitchen and bathroom are in. Nobody has anywhere to sleep or sit yet.
tenant.name: Marisol

mechanic_intro.body:
Dani's flat is empty, and Dani needs a lot. The bar at the bottom lists it: a cross for every need the flat doesn't meet yet, a tick once it does.

Each need ticks as soon as there is a piece that provides it: a bed to sleep in, a toilet or a sink to wash, a stove to cook on, a desk to work at and a chair to sit on. The freezers are one need of their own: it counts them, and ticks once all three are in.

Open Furniture: the catalogue starts on what is still missing. There is room and money for all of it. Short on floor anyway? A Loft Bed sleeps above head height, and a low chest freezer fits under it.
mechanic_intro.title: The basic needs

tenant.flavor: Streams twelve hours a day and buys frozen pizza by the pallet. Needs three freezers, and is not negotiating.
tenant.name: Dani

mechanic_intro.body:
Some tenants need the apartment to be two different places. The tabs at the bottom are Moments: here, Day and Night. Each has its own list of needs, and every Moment has to be satisfied.

Convertible furniture is how one room does both jobs. A sofa bed or a futon is a seat when folded and a bed when unfolded. Click one to fold or unfold it, and each Moment remembers its own state.

The budget won't stretch to a sofa and a bed. Buy one piece that is both, switch to Night, and unfold it.
mechanic_intro.title: Moments

tenant.flavor: Works from the sofa all day and needs the same four walls to be a bedroom at night.
tenant.name: Noor

mechanic_intro.body:
Everything with a heart belonged to Irene's grandmother. It stays in the flat. It does not have to stay where it is.

Irene needs a desk and a chair, and there is no clear spot for them. Rearrange the inheritance until there is.
mechanic_intro.title: Furniture that cannot leave

tenant.flavor: Moved into her grandmother's flat with all of her grandmother's furniture. None of it is leaving. She still needs somewhere to work.
tenant.name: Irene

mechanic_intro.body:
Achís changes personality whenever she sneezes, and each personality is a Moment with its own needs.

Nothing is bought three times over. Find the pieces that serve more than one of her, and check every Moment before you call it done.
mechanic_intro.title: Three people, one room

tenant.flavor: Every time she sneezes she becomes someone else: a bookworm, a host, a sleepyhead. All three live in the same room.
tenant.name: Achís

mechanic_intro.body:
The tower has four floors and each one is barely two metres across. The staircase eats a third of every one of them.

No floor can hold a whole home, so spread it out: one or two needs per floor. Use the floor tabs at the bottom right, or the Up and Down arrow keys, to move between them.
mechanic_intro.title: Many floors, all of them narrow

tenant.flavor: Bought a medieval watchtower: four floors, each two metres across. He wants a whole home in it.
tenant.name: Sir Guillem

mechanic_intro.body:
Some needs are not furniture: they are whether one spot can see another. Tall furniture blocks a line of sight, low furniture doesn't.

The parents want two lines kept clear. Their daughter wants one line blocked: nobody should see her window from her doorway. The three lines are numbered and drawn in both views: green when the rule is met, red when it is not. A solid line has to stay clear; a dashed line has to be blocked.

A wardrobe in the wrong place breaks a line. A wardrobe in the right place is exactly what she needs.
mechanic_intro.title: Lines of sight

tenant.flavor: They want to see the front door from the sofa and their daughter's doorway from the computer. Their daughter wants the window where they can't see it.
tenant.name: The Ferrers

sightline_requirements.label: See the front door from the sofa corner
See the daughter's doorway from the computer corner
The window can't be seen from her doorway

mechanic_intro.body:
A zone is a stretch of floor you can walk across without passing through anything tall. An open doorway joins two rooms into one zone.

The by-law says sleeping and cooking must be in different zones. The two halves of this house are joined by an opening in the border wall, so right now they are one.

Tall storage (a bookshelf, a wardrobe) works as a divider. Close the opening with one, and the house becomes two zones.
mechanic_intro.title: Zones

tenant.flavor: The town line runs through her living room. One council's by-law: nobody sleeps in the same room as a kitchen. The other council owns the kitchen.
tenant.name: Bruna

tenant.flavor: Debug level for moments + free space. Day needs enough open floor to work out ('sport'); Night needs the Sofa Bed unfolded to sleep. Fold it away by day to free up the room.
tenant.name: Debug Tenant

tenant.flavor: Debug level for the rails mechanic. The Wardrobe slides horizontally along its rail (drag it left/right), the Bookshelf slides vertically along its own rail. Buy a fresh Wardrobe/Bookshelf from the shop to see it slide freely (no bounds) along whichever row/column you drop it on.
tenant.name: Debug Tenant

tenant.flavor: Debug level for rails + moments together. The Wardrobe hides flush against the wall on its rail. During Dress Up, slide it right into the marked reveal zone to fulfill "dress" -- slide it back for Normal, where it just looks like a closet door.
tenant.name: Debug Tenant

tenant.flavor: Debug level for wall demolition: the room starts split in two by a non-load-bearing partition (dashed, demolishable) between two solid load-bearing walls (hatched, permanent). Demolish the partition during the pre-furnish phase to open up the full room.
tenant.name: Debug Tenant

tenant.flavor: Debug level for the balcony floor_kind: tiles south of the main wall are tagged "balcony" so they render as open exterior floor with railings on the exposed edges (no walls of their own) instead of a normal walled room.
tenant.name: Debug Tenant

tenant.flavor: Debug level for the animated Balcony Window (foldable wall item, id "balcony_window"). Top wall (y=1) runs the full 38 tiles so the 17-tile-wide item fits with room to spare; the room is 34 tiles deep so the 11-tile balcony extension has clearance to open without hitting the opposite wall. Big budget (6000) covers its 3500 buy price plus the starting toilet/sink used only to satisfy the required "hygiene" function.
tenant.name: Debug Tenant

tenant.flavor: Needs a proper home.
tenant.name: Alex

tenant.flavor: QA showcase: L-shaped multi-room floor, interior wall + door, window, column, sloped ceiling, bathroom floor-kind zone, kitchen, living room, office, rail wardrobe with a day/night dress reveal, and full subfloor/ceiling layers. Buy a staircase anywhere to test the loft/multi-level mechanic.
tenant.name: QA Tester

tenant.flavor: Tiny apartment inside a shoebox, inside another apartment. Its window's daylight depends on what the OUTER apartment placed in front of the box. It also has its OWN shoebox — a second level of nesting, to prove the recursion works.
tenant.name: (nested)

tenant.flavor: A shoebox inside a shoebox inside an apartment. If you can see this, recursive nesting works.
tenant.name: (nested x2)

tenant.flavor: Debug level exercising all 5 new mechanics at once: the shoebox (nested level) has its light blocked by the adjacent wardrobe (tall furniture); the desk+lamp demonstrate weight/support; a sightline requirement and an external-zone boundary restriction are also active.
tenant.name: (debug)

sightline_requirements.label: ver el amanecer desde el escritorio

tenant.flavor: Tiny apartment inside a shoebox, inside another apartment. Its window's daylight depends on what the OUTER apartment placed in front of the box. It also has its OWN shoebox — a second level of nesting, to prove the recursion works.
tenant.name: (nested)

tenant.flavor: Debug level for the 3 mobility tiers + Moments. Sofa = red (shares one position across every Moment — try dragging it, watch the notice, then try dragging it onto wherever the chair sits in the OTHER moment to see it get blocked). Wardrobe = red but on a rail (still slides per-Moment, the exception). Desk & Dresser = yellow (watch the comfort meter appear/drop as you move them away from their starting spot, and recover if you move them back — move both far enough to see the 'can't be solved' warning). Chair & Stool = green (freely movable, can sit somewhere different in each Moment, no comfort cost).
tenant.name: Debug Tenant

tenant.flavor: Debug level for furniture stacking. The Desk (capacity 6) and Nightstand (capacity 8) are both valid surfaces. Buy small items (Desk Lamp, Square Table Lamp, Book Stack, weight ~1) from the shop and stack a few on either surface — they should fit and the surface's remaining capacity goes down each time. Then try stacking something heavier (a Stool, weight 9, or anything bigger) — it should be rejected with a 'would break' message and the exact numbers. Bare floor placement is unaffected either way.
tenant.name: Debug Tenant

tenant.flavor: Debug level for sightlines (height-based blocking). Two requirements, testing BOTH directions: 1) 'See the sunrise' from the desk to the window MUST be clear — the Wardrobe (tall) currently blocks it, move it out of the way. 2) 'Overprotective parents' from the door to the bed nook must STAY blocked — the Bookshelf (tall) currently blocks it correctly; try moving the bookshelf away and watch this requirement fail.
tenant.name: Debug Tenant

sightline_requirements.label: See the sunrise from the desk
Overprotective parents can't see the bed nook

mechanic_intro.body:
This flat has no outside on two sides. Walk out of the west wall (A) and you come in through the east one. The opening marked B in the north wall leads back in through the B in the south wall: same letter, same doorway.

Furniture can stand across a seam: the sofa is half on each side. A piece longer than the loop runs into its own tail, so the 2.4 m kitchen won't go east-west here. Light, lines of sight and the tenant all go through the seams too.
mechanic_intro.title: A looped flat

tenant.flavor: Took the flat because the hallway goes on for ever. Needs a bed, a kitchen and somewhere to put things, in a flat that is 2.3 m wide and also endless.
tenant.name: Moebius

tenant.flavor: A bed, a lamp, a door that locks. He is only here to sleep.
tenant.name: Kenji

tenant.flavor: First room of her own. The desk matters more than the bed.
tenant.name: Imke

tenant.flavor: They split the rent three ways and are gone by Friday.
tenant.name: Three backpackers

tenant.flavor: Paints at night, sleeps at noon, pays on time.
tenant.name: Odile

tenant.flavor: Works nights at the harbour. Needs it dark and quiet by day.
tenant.name: Tomasz

tenant.flavor: Saving for a place of their own. This will do until then.
tenant.name: Lena and Aron

tenant.flavor: Two parents, two children, one room. They have done the sums.
tenant.name: The Baumanns

tenant.flavor: Insists it is a penthouse. Pays as if it were one.
tenant.name: Frau von Hagen

tenant.flavor: Translates novels under the roof tiles. Her bed is already up here; everything tall has to go where she can stand.
tenant.name: Ines

tenant.flavor: Sleeps up on the platform, lounges down in the pit. Wants a desk and somewhere for his things, and the steps kept clear.
tenant.name: Theo
